quizName: DMV Practice Test #4 25 Questions • Passing Score 19

questions.question: What color are warning signs?

options.text: Yellow with black lettering or symbols
Blue with white lettering
Red with white lettering
White with black numbers

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow with black lettering or symbols
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: How long does a pre-ride inspection take?

options.text: A few minutes, done once a month
A few minutes, done before every ride
Over an hour, done by a mechanic
Over an hour, only when carrying a passenger

questions.correctAnswerText: A few minutes, done before every ride
questions.explanation: Do a quick pre-ride inspection before every ride. It takes only a few minutes.

questions.question: What should you do while riding?

options.text: Always look ahead and watch for dangers
Focus on your speedometer and controls instead of the road
Do not worry about hazards on the road
Look ahead but avoid looking for hazards

questions.correctAnswerText: Always look ahead and watch for dangers
questions.explanation: Always look well ahead to spot dangers early. This helps you react before you reach a hazard.

questions.question: Which material protects motorcycle riders the best?

options.text: Leather
Denim
Polyester
Wool

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather
questions.explanation: Leather jackets and pants offer the most protection for motorcycle riders.

questions.question: What is NOT required on a DOT-approved helmet?

options.text: An outer shell that resists impact
An inner lining that absorbs impact
A chinstrap system
Bright painted colors on the outside

questions.correctAnswerText: Bright painted colors on the outside
questions.explanation: A DOT-approved helmet must have an impact-resistant outer shell, an impact-absorbing inner lining, a comfort liner, and a chinstrap system. Bright colors are not required.

questions.question: When does a motorcycle fit you properly?

options.text: When your feet can touch the ground while sitting
When you can reach the controls by stretching
When the handlebars are above your head
When your feet cannot rest on the foot pegs

questions.correctAnswerText: When your feet can touch the ground while sitting
questions.explanation: A motorcycle fits properly when your feet reach the ground while you sit on it. You should easily reach and operate all controls.

questions.question: How can you lower your crash risk?

options.text: Tell other drivers what you plan to do
Don't look ahead while riding
Wear dark clothing
Ride where it is hard for others to see you

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell other drivers what you plan to do
questions.explanation: Reduce crash risk by staying visible. Use your turn signals, brake light, and proper lane position. Scan the road around you and keep space between your motorcycle and other vehicles.

questions.question: When hitting a bump or pothole, why should you rise off your seat?

options.text: So you can jump off if needed
So your legs can absorb the shock
So other drivers can see you
So you can see the uneven surface better

questions.correctAnswerText: So your legs can absorb the shock
questions.explanation: Rising off your seat lets your joints absorb impact. This prevents the shock from throwing you off the motorcycle.

questions.question: Where should you find information about your motorcycle?

options.text: The owner's manual
A general motorcycle book
The previous owner
Someone who knows about motorcycles

questions.correctAnswerText: The owner's manual
questions.explanation: Your owner's manual is the best source for information about your specific motorcycle. It includes specifications, how to operate it, and maintenance information.

questions.question: How can you be more visible on your motorcycle?

options.text: Add extra lights to your motorcycle
Don't use your turn signal
Wear dark clothes
Wave at people

questions.correctAnswerText: Add extra lights to your motorcycle
questions.explanation: Increase visibility by wearing bright or reflective clothing. Add extra lights to your motorcycle, use your turn signals, and flash your brake light when needed.

questions.question: Intersections are usually:

options.text: Safe because there is a lot of traffic.
Dangerous for motorcycle riders.
Hard to understand.
Safer than open roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dangerous for motorcycle riders.
questions.explanation: Intersections are dangerous because many conflicts can happen between motorcycles and other vehicles.

questions.question: If you borrow a motorcycle:

options.text: You don't need to check the tire pressure.
It will handle the same as your own bike.
The owner will check the brakes for you.
Leave extra space between you and other vehicles so you have more time to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave extra space between you and other vehicles so you have more time to stop.
questions.explanation: Check the motorcycle before riding, just like you would your own bike. Ride carefully on an unfamiliar motorcycle and keep extra distance from other vehicles.

questions.question: If someone is tailgating you, you should:

options.text: Ride faster to get away.
Call the police.
Ride on the road shoulder.
Let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to let them get ahead. Change lanes safely and let them pass. Riding faster may make things more dangerous.

questions.question: Riding at night:

options.text: Should be avoided.
Is safer when you wear reflective clothing.
Is unsafe because other drivers cannot see your turn signals.
Should only happen in cities.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is safer when you wear reflective clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear reflective clothing at night to make yourself more visible to other drivers.

questions.question: When riding in a vehicle's blind spot, you should:

options.text: Stay where you are so you don't surprise the driver.
Wave at the driver to get their attention.
Slow down to move out of the blind spot.
Pull over to the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to move out of the blind spot.
questions.explanation: If you are in a vehicle's blind spot, either speed up quickly or slow down to leave that spot.

questions.question: Taking a turn too fast:

options.text: Is okay as long as you stay under the speed limit.
Is safer on a motorcycle than in a car.
Is okay if no other vehicles are nearby.
Can make you drift into another lane or off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can make you drift into another lane or off the road.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast is dangerous. You may drift into another lane or off the road. Always slow down before turning.

questions.question: What is the best footwear for a motorcycle rider?

options.text: Sturdy boots
Tennis shoes
Shoes with loose laces
Sandals

questions.correctAnswerText: Sturdy boots
questions.explanation: Sturdy boots or shoes that cover the ankles provide the best protection. Laced-up boots are best. If your shoes have long laces, tuck them in securely before riding.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white background and black letters. Follow all rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to handle differently while riding, you should:

options.text: Keep riding normally.
Pull over and check the tires.
Pull over to check the chain.
Pull over to check the windshield.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and check the tires.
questions.explanation: A sudden change in handling may mean a tire has failed. If your motorcycle feels different, pull over safely and check your tires.

questions.question: Taking corners too fast:

options.text: Can cause you to drift into another lane.
Is better than going too slowly.
Usually keeps you in your lane.
Is okay because motorcycles are smaller.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can cause you to drift into another lane.
questions.explanation: Taking a corner too fast may cause you to drift into another lane or off the road. Slow down before you start to turn.

questions.question: A cushion of space while riding helps you:

options.text: Have time to react to hazards.
Stay hidden from other drivers.
Get stuck and unable to avoid hazards.
Read road signs more easily.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have time to react to hazards.
questions.explanation: Keep space around your motorcycle at all times. This gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake. You need this space to turn safely.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Stay farther behind other vehicles.
Go faster.
Let air out of the tires for the extra weight.
Not tell your passenger about dangers ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind other vehicles.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle handles differently with a passenger's weight. Keep more distance between you and other vehicles when carrying someone else.

questions.question: For the best protection, your helmet should:

options.text: Meet Department of Transportation standards.
Look strong.
Cost very little.
Be your favorite color.

questions.correctAnswerText: Meet Department of Transportation standards.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. It should fit snugly around your entire head with no visible damage.

questions.question: Which item is NOT protective clothing for a motorcyclist?

options.text: A jacket
Boots
Gloves
A stocking cap

questions.correctAnswerText: A stocking cap
questions.explanation: Wear protective clothing when riding. This includes sturdy pants and jackets that cover your arms and legs, boots or heavy shoes that cover your ankles, and sturdy gloves.

questions.question: The shortest and safest stops happen when you:

options.text: Use only the rear brake.
Use only the front brake.
Let the front tire lock up.
Use both the front and rear brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both the front and rear brakes together in a smooth, gradual way to stop safely. Do not let either tire skid.
